question: In Arizona, a CDL is required to operate a single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of at least how many pounds?
explanation: The manual states you must have a CDL to operate any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 26,001 pounds or more.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A CDL is required for a combination vehicle with a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the towed unit's GVWR exceeds what weight?
explanation: A combination vehicle needs a CDL if it has a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) is in excess of 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A CDL is required to drive a vehicle designed to transport how many or more passengers, including the driver?
explanation: The manual specifies a CDL is required for a vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A CDL is required for any size vehicle that:
choice_a: Is used only within city limits
choice_c: Is towed behind a personal pickup truck
explanation: A CDL is required for any size vehicle which requires hazardous material placards or is carrying material listed as a select agent or toxin, regardless of the vehicle's weight.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: What is the minimum age to apply for an Arizona CDL that is valid only for intrastate (within Arizona) driving?
explanation: The minimum age for a commercial driver license is 21, but if you are at least 18, you may apply for an intrastate commercial driver license valid only in Arizona.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 6

question: Drivers under the age of 21 who hold a CDL or CLP are prohibited from:
choice_c: Transporting placarded amounts of hazardous materials
choice_d: Operating a vehicle with air brakes
explanation: Drivers under the age of 21 are prohibited from transporting placarded amounts of Hazardous Materials, even if they otherwise qualify for a CDL or CLP.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 8

question: How long is an Arizona Commercial Learner Permit (CLP) valid?
explanation: The commercial learner permit is valid for a 12-month period.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 8

question: How often must a CDL or CLP holder's Medical Examiner Certificate be renewed, at minimum?
explanation: The Medical Examiner Certificate is to be renewed every 24 months or sooner, as determined by the medical examiner or by regulation.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 7

question: If a CDL holder's license remains suspended or revoked for 12 months or more, what must they do to drive commercially again?
choice_a: Nothing extra, the CDL reactivates automatically
choice_d: Retake all CDL written, vision, and skills tests, and submit a new medical exam form
explanation: A CDL holder that remains suspended or revoked for 12 months or more will be required to retake all CDL written, vision, and demonstration-skill tests, submit the medical examination form, and pay all applicable fees.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 7

question: To obtain an unrestricted Arizona CDL, an applicant's uncorrected vision must be at least:
explanation: You must have uncorrected vision of 20/40 or better in each eye to obtain an unrestricted license; otherwise a 'B' restriction requiring glasses or contacts is issued.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 12

question: What minimum score must an applicant achieve on each CDL knowledge test to pass?
explanation: The applicant must answer at least 80 percent of the questions correctly on each knowledge test to achieve a passing score.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 9

question: If you fail a CDL knowledge test, when are you allowed to retake it?
choice_d: Immediately, as many times as needed the same day
explanation: Applicants must wait until the next business day to retake any failed knowledge tests.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 9

question: A Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) holder is not eligible to take the CDL Skills Test within how many days of the initial issuance of the CLP?
explanation: A CLP holder is not eligible to take the CDL Skills Test within 14 days of the initial issuance of the Commercial Learner's Permit.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 9

question: Which CDL knowledge test must be taken by all applicants, regardless of the class of license sought?
explanation: The general knowledge test is taken by all applicants, regardless of the class of license or endorsements sought.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: What are the three types of general skills tests required for a CDL?
choice_b: Air brake test, coupling test, and cargo test
choice_c: Backing test, parking test, and highway test
choice_d: Vehicle Inspection Test, Basic Control Skills Test, and Road Test
explanation: There are three types of general skills tests: the Vehicle Inspection Test (VIT), Basic Control Skills Test (BCST), and Road Test (RT).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: The tank vehicle test is required if you want to haul liquid or gaseous material in a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of at least:
explanation: The tank vehicle test is required for tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, whether permanently or temporarily attached.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A driver who certifies as 'Interstate non-excepted' is stating that they:
choice_c: Are subject to and must meet Federal DOT medical card requirements
choice_d: Are exempt from all medical certification
explanation: The Interstate non-excepted certification states you operate or expect to operate in interstate commerce, are subject to and meet the Federal DOT medical card requirements under 49 CFR part 391, and must obtain a medical examiner's certificate.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-4

question: A Transportation Security Administration (TSA) Security Threat Assessment (STA), required for a Hazardous Materials endorsement, is valid for how long from the date of completion?
explanation: A Security Threat Assessment (STA) is good for 5 years from the date of completion.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 9

question: It is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at or above:
explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is .04% or more.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-4

question: For a first offense of driving a CMV with a BAC of .04% or more, a driver will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: A driver will lose their CDL for at least one year for a first offense of driving a CMV with a BAC of .04% or higher, among other listed offenses.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-4

question: If a disqualifying alcohol-related offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials, the minimum CDL loss for a first offense increases to:
explanation: A driver will lose their CDL for at least three years if the offense occurs while operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-4

question: A driver found to have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% will be:
explanation: A driver will be put out-of-service for 24 hours if they have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04%.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: Under the CDL disqualification rules, 'excessive speeding' is defined as driving how many mph or more above the posted speed limit?
explanation: Excessive speeding is defined as 15 mph or more above the posted limit and is classified as a serious traffic violation.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: A driver who commits two serious traffic violations within a three-year period while operating a CMV will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: A driver will lose their CDL for at least 60 days for committing two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: A driver who commits a first violation of an out-of-service order will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: A driver will lose their CDL for at least 180 days for a first violation of an out-of-service order.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: For a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation (such as failing to stop when required), a CDL holder will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: A driver loses their CDL for at least 60 days for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation, such as failing to stop before the crossing when required.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: A driver may not hold more than one driver license. Violating this rule can result in a court fine of up to:
explanation: If you break the rule against holding more than one license, a court may fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail, and your other licenses will be surrendered.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-6

question: Using a hand-held mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication while driving a CMV includes which of the following?
choice_a: Using a pre-programmed voice-activated dialing feature
choice_b: Dialing a mobile telephone by pressing more than a single button
choice_c: Leaving the phone mounted in a dashboard cradle
explanation: The use of a hand-held mobile telephone includes dialing a mobile telephone by pressing more than a single button, as well as holding it to talk or reaching for it while unrestrained by the seat belt.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-6

question: Under the International Registration Plan (IRP), a 'Qualified Vehicle' generally includes a power unit with two axles and a gross vehicle weight in excess of:
explanation: A Qualified Vehicle under IRP includes a power unit with two axles and a gross vehicle weight or registered gross vehicle weight in excess of 26,000 pounds, or three or more axles regardless of weight.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: An Arizona CDL is generally issued for how many years, except in certain cases?
explanation: Arizona issues an 8-year Commercial Driver License (CDL), except in certain cases, and drivers may renew up to six months prior to expiration.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Customer Service Guide for Commercial Drivers, p. 10
